question.question:
A company's GHG inventory reports base-year Scope 1 plus Scope 2 emissions E0=119000 tons CO2e. During the reporting period it acquired a business whose base-year emissions were A=9700 tons CO2e; the current-year inventory already includes the acquired business. Base-year recalculation policy: if A divided by E0 is at least the significance threshold s=5.25 percent (exactly at the threshold triggers recalculation), the base year is recalculated to E0 plus A; otherwise the base year stays E0. The company's target is to cut emissions by R=42 percent below the (possibly recalculated) base-year emissions by the target year, N=8 years after the base year, following a straight-line pathway from base-year emissions to the target-year level. The current reporting year is k=2 years after the base year, with reported emissions C=86500 tons CO2e. Excess over pathway is current emissions minus the pathway allowance for year k, positive when above the pathway. Compute the constant annual percentage reduction that, applied to C and compounding each year over the remaining N minus k years, lands exactly on the target-year level. Use exact arithmetic for all tonnage quantities and round only the final percentage half up to two decimal places.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `percent` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Whether the recalculation policy is triggered.
Exact base-year emissions after policy applied.
Exact straight-line pathway allowance for current year.
Exact signed current emissions above pathway allowance.
